events.region: Guam, GU
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central and northern Guam...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM ChST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways possible. Some low-water crossings may become
impassable. Rises in small streams.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 704 AM ChST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Dededo, Tamuning, Yigo, Mangilao, Chalan Pago-Ordot, Barrigada,
Hagatna Heights, Andersen AFB, Mongmong-Toto-Maite and Sinajana.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Copiah, MS; Franklin, MS; Lincoln, MS
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SVRJAN

The National Weather Service in Jackson has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Lincoln County in south central Mississippi...
Eastern Franklin County in southwestern Mississippi...
Southwestern Copiah County in central Mississippi...

* Until 500 PM CDT.

* At 402 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located over Brookhaven,
moving west at 20 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* This severe thunderstorm will be near...
West Lincoln, Vaughn, and Loyd Star around 410 PM CDT.
Mccall Creek around 425 PM CDT.

events.region: Waters from Cape Blanco OR to Pt. St. George CA from 10 to 60 nm
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisories, north winds 20 to 30 kt
and steep seas 6 to 9 ft at 7 seconds. For the Hazardous Seas
Warning, north winds 20 to 30 kt with occasional gusts to 35 kt
and very steep and hazardous seas 8 to 11 ft at 8 seconds
expected.

* WHERE...All of the area. Steepest seas will occur this evening
and overnight beyond 10 nm from shore south of Port Orford.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 5 PM PDT this
afternoon. For the Hazardous Seas Warning, from 5 PM this
afternoon to 5 AM PDT Wednesday. For the Small Craft Advisory,
from 5 AM to 8 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Steep to very steep and hazardous seas could capsize
or damage vessels.

* View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northern Ventura County in southwestern California...

* WHEN...Until 500 PM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 154 PM PDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to nearly stationary thunderstorms. This will
cause arroyo and small stream flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lockwood Valley, Frazier Mountain, Alamo Mountain and Highway 33
from Lockwood Valley Road to the Santa Barbara County line.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 3 to 6 feet with sets up to 8
feet, highest at south and southwest-facing beaches. Strong
and dangerous rip and longshore currents. Minor coastal
flooding from a combination of high surf and high astronomical
tides during the evenings.

* WHERE...Beaches of Orange and San Diego Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 PM PDT
Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 11 PM PDT this
evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with isolated
road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...While surf diminishes gradually into
Wednesday, the high astronomical tides linger into mid-week
which could continue to bring minor coastal flooding during
evening high tides. Predicted higher high tides: Newport Beach:
7.0 feet at 7:59 PM. La Jolla: 6.9 feet at 7:54 PM.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Extreme Heat Warning, dangerously hot conditions
with high temperatures in the mid 80s at the beaches to 90s for
higher coastal terrain with low temperatures in the lower to mid
70s. For the Heat Advisory, high temperatures around 80 near the
coast to the lower to mid 90s for higher coastal terrain.

* WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas and San Diego County Coastal
Areas.

* WHEN...For the Extreme Heat Warning, until 8 PM PDT Wednesday. For
the Heat Advisory, from 8 PM Wednesday to 8 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Major to Extreme HeatRisk through Wednesday.
Warm overnight low temperature will limit relief from the heat.
